documents.title: Halden Labs Information Security Program: Policy review
documents.text:
## Policy review
All security policies are reviewed at least once per year, and immediately when a significant change in systems, law or risk occurs.

documents.title: Halden Labs Information Security Program: Audits
documents.text:
## Audits
Internal security audits are performed quarterly by the Security & IT team and cover the whole program.
An independent third-party auditor performs a SOC 2 Type II audit every year covering all systems used to deliver the service. A management summary of the latest report is shared with customers under NDA.

documents.title: Halden Labs Information Security Program: Risk management
documents.text:
## Risk management
Risk assessments are reviewed and updated twice per year, and after any major incident.

documents.title: Halden Labs Information Security Program: Training
documents.text:
## Training
All employees complete security and privacy training during onboarding and then every year. Contractors and interns with system access complete the same training before access is granted.

documents.title: Halden Labs Information Security Program: Personnel
documents.text:
## Personnel
Background checks are performed for employees in Engineering and Customer Support before they are granted access to production systems or customer data. Other roles are checked where local law allows.
Violations of security policy are handled through the HR disciplinary process.

documents.title: Halden Labs Access Control Policy: Principles
documents.text:
## Principles
Access to systems and data is granted on a need-to-know and least-privilege basis. Every access request must name the system, the access level and a business reason, and is approved by the requester's manager and the system owner.

documents.title: Halden Labs Access Control Policy: Authentication
documents.text:
## Authentication
All workforce accounts use single sign-on with phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication.
Customer-facing passwords must be at least 12 characters and are checked against a list of breached passwords. Passwords are stored only as salted hashes using bcrypt.
User sessions in the Halden web application expire after 30 minutes of inactivity.

documents.title: Halden Labs Access Control Policy: Administrative access
documents.text:
## Administrative access
Administrators use a separate privileged account for administrative work and a standard account for email and daily tasks. Production servers are reached through a bastion host with personal accounts; shared root logins are disabled and elevation uses sudo.
Administrative access to production is reviewed every quarter by the system owners.

documents.title: Halden Labs Access Control Policy: Joiners, movers and leavers
documents.text:
## Joiners, movers and leavers
When an employee, contractor or intern leaves, HR raises an offboarding ticket and all logical access is revoked within 24 hours. Badges for the office are deactivated on the last working day.

documents.title: Halden Labs Logging and Monitoring Standard: What is logged
documents.text:
## What is logged
Production servers, network devices and identity systems log security-relevant events, including sign-ins, privilege changes and access to customer data. Company laptops send endpoint security events to the endpoint protection console.

documents.title: Halden Labs Logging and Monitoring Standard: Where logs go
documents.text:
## Where logs go
All production and network logs are forwarded to a central log platform. Engineers cannot delete or edit forwarded logs.

documents.title: Halden Labs Logging and Monitoring Standard: Retention
documents.text:
## Retention
Security event logs are retained for 90 days in the central log platform and then deleted.

documents.title: Halden Labs Logging and Monitoring Standard: Monitoring
documents.text:
## Monitoring
Network and service availability is monitored around the clock, with alerts paged to the on-call engineer. Security alerts from the log platform are triaged by the Security & IT team every business day.

documents.title: Halden Labs Incident Response Plan: Documented procedures
documents.text:
## Documented procedures
This plan documents how Halden Labs detects, triages, contains, investigates and recovers from security incidents. It is tested in a tabletop exercise twice a year.

documents.title: Halden Labs Incident Response Plan: Investigation
documents.text:
## Investigation
Halden Labs maintains an internal incident response team with forensics tooling and can conduct investigations without outside help. An external forensics firm is on retainer for major incidents.

documents.title: Halden Labs Incident Response Plan: Evidence
documents.text:
## Evidence
To support investigations, security logs are retained for 12 months.

documents.title: Halden Labs Incident Response Plan: Customer notification
documents.text:
## Customer notification
Affected customers are notified without undue delay, and in any case within 72 hours of confirming a security incident that affects their data.

documents.title: Halden Labs Incident Response Plan: Vulnerability reports
documents.text:
## Vulnerability reports
External researchers can report vulnerabilities to security@halden.example. Reports are acknowledged within two business days and triaged by the Security & IT team.

documents.title: Halden Labs Infrastructure Security Standard: Hosting
documents.text:
## Hosting
The Halden platform runs entirely in a major public cloud provider's data centers. Halden Labs does not operate its own data centers; physical security of those facilities is the provider's responsibility and is covered by the provider's SOC 2 report.

documents.title: Halden Labs Infrastructure Security Standard: Network
documents.text:
## Network
Cloud security groups and a managed web application firewall restrict inbound and outbound traffic. Internet-facing services sit in a separate public subnet; databases and internal services run in private subnets with no public addresses.
All traffic between services is encrypted with TLS 1.2 or higher, including traffic inside the private network. The TLS configuration is reviewed every quarter and only modern cipher suites are enabled.
Employees reach internal tools through a zero-trust access proxy. Halden Labs does not operate a traditional VPN.

documents.title: Halden Labs Infrastructure Security Standard: Hardening and patching
documents.text:
## Hardening and patching
Servers are built from hardened, versioned images defined in code. Security patches are applied monthly. Critical vulnerabilities are patched within 72 hours under an emergency change.

documents.title: Halden Labs Infrastructure Security Standard: Backups
documents.text:
## Backups
Production databases are backed up continuously to a second cloud region. Restores are tested every quarter.

documents.title: Halden Labs Infrastructure Security Standard: Testing
documents.text:
## Testing
An independent firm performs a manual penetration test of the platform once a year. Automated vulnerability scans of all production hosts run weekly.

documents.title: Halden Labs Infrastructure Security Standard: Change management
documents.text:
## Change management
Production changes go through a documented change process. Changes are classified as standard, normal or emergency by impact, and every change record is retained.

documents.title: Halden Labs Endpoint and Vendor Security Policy: Company devices
documents.text:
## Company devices
All company laptops are managed by the device management platform, have full-disk encryption turned on and run endpoint malware protection.
Phones may access company email only after enrolment in device management, which enforces device encryption and a passcode. Unenrolled or unencrypted mobile devices are blocked.

documents.title: Halden Labs Endpoint and Vendor Security Policy: Vendors
documents.text:
## Vendors
The Security & IT team reviews every service provider that will store or process customer data before contract signature, and again every year.
Contracts with these providers require them to protect the security and confidentiality of customer data at least to the standard of this program.

documents.title: Halden Labs Information Security Program: Policy review

documents.title: Halden Labs Information Security Program: Audits

documents.title: Halden Labs Access Control Policy: Principles
documents.text:
## Principles

documents.title: Halden Labs Access Control Policy: Authentication
documents.text:
## Authentication
All workforce accounts use single sign-on with phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication.
Customer-facing passwords must be at least 12 characters and are checked against a list of breached passwords. Passwords are stored only as salted hashes using bcrypt.
User sessions in the Halden web application expire after 30 minutes of inactivity.

documents.title: Halden Labs Access Control Policy: Administrative access
documents.text:

documents.title: Halden Labs Logging and Monitoring Standard: Where logs go
documents.text:

All production and network logs are forwarded to a central log platform. Engineers cannot delete or edit forwarded logs.

documents.title: Halden Labs Logging and Monitoring Standard: Retention
documents.text:

documents.title: Halden Labs Logging and Monitoring Standard: Monitoring
documents.text:

documents.title: Halden Labs Incident Response Plan: Documented procedures
documents.text:
## Documented procedures
This plan documents how Halden Labs detects, triages, contains, investigates and recovers from security incidents. It is tested in a tabletop exercise twice a year.

documents.title: Halden Labs Incident Response Plan: Investigation
documents.text:
## Investigation
Halden Labs maintains an internal incident response team with forensics tooling and can conduct investigations without outside help. An external forensics firm is on retainer for major incidents.

documents.title: Halden Labs Incident Response Plan: Evidence
documents.text:
## Evidence
To support investigations, security logs are retained for 12 months.

documents.title: Halden Labs Incident Response Plan: Customer notification
documents.text:
## Customer notification
Affected customers are notified without undue delay, and in any case within 72 hours of confirming a security incident that affects their data.

documents.title: Halden Labs Incident Response Plan: Vulnerability reports
documents.text:
## Vulnerability reports
External researchers can report vulnerabilities to security@halden.example. Reports are acknowledged within two business days and triaged by the Security & IT team.

documents.title: Halden Labs Infrastructure Security Standard: Hosting
documents.text:
## Hosting
The Halden platform runs entirely in a major public cloud provider's data centers. Halden Labs does not operate its own data centers; physical security of those facilities is the provider's responsibility and is covered by the provider's SOC 2 report.

documents.title: Halden Labs Infrastructure Security Standard: Network
documents.text:
## Network
Cloud security groups and a managed web application firewall restrict inbound and outbound traffic. Internet-facing services sit in a separate public subnet; databases and internal services run in private subnets with no public addresses.
All traffic between services is encrypted with TLS 1.2 or higher, including traffic inside the private network. The TLS configuration is reviewed every quarter and only modern cipher suites are enabled.
Employees reach internal tools through a zero-trust access proxy. Halden Labs does not operate a traditional VPN.

documents.title: Halden Labs Infrastructure Security Standard: Hardening and patching
documents.text:
## Hardening and patching
Servers are built from hardened, versioned images defined in code. Security patches are applied monthly. Critical vulnerabilities are patched within 72 hours under an emergency change.

documents.title: Halden Labs Infrastructure Security Standard: Backups
documents.text:
## Backups
Production databases are backed up continuously to a second cloud region. Restores are tested every quarter.

documents.title: Halden Labs Infrastructure Security Standard: Testing
documents.text:
## Testing
An independent firm performs a manual penetration test of the platform once a year. Automated vulnerability scans of all production hosts run weekly.

documents.title: Halden Labs Infrastructure Security Standard: Change management
documents.text:
## Change management
Production changes go through a documented change process. Changes are classified as standard, normal or emergency by impact, and every change record is retained.

documents.title: Halden Labs Endpoint and Vendor Security Policy: Company devices
documents.text:
## Company devices
All company laptops are managed by the device management platform, have full-disk encryption turned on and run endpoint malware protection.
Phones may access company email only after enrolment in device management, which enforces device encryption and a passcode. Unenrolled or unencrypted mobile devices are blocked.

documents.title: Halden Labs Endpoint and Vendor Security Policy: Vendors
documents.text:
## Vendors
The Security & IT team reviews every service provider that will store or process customer data before contract signature, and again every year.
Contracts with these providers require them to protect the security and confidentiality of customer data at least to the standard of this program.

## Documented procedures
This plan documents how Halden Labs detects, triages, contains, investigates and recovers from security incidents. It is tested in a tabletop exercise twice a year.

## Vulnerability reports
External researchers can report vulnerabilities to security@halden.example. Reports are acknowledged within two business days and triaged by the Security & IT team.

## Customer notification
Affected customers are notified without undue delay, and in any case within 72 hours of confirming a security incident that affects their data.

Administrators use a separate privileged account for administrative work and a standard account for email and daily tasks. Production servers are reached through a bastion host with personal accounts; shared root logins are disabled and elevation uses sudo.
Administrative access to production is reviewed every quarter by the system owners.

documents.title: Halden Labs Access Control Policy: Joiners, movers and leavers
documents.text:
## Joiners, movers and leavers
When an employee, contractor or intern leaves, HR raises an offboarding ticket and all logical access is revoked within 24 hours. Badges for the office are deactivated on the last working day.

documents.title: Halden Labs Logging and Monitoring Standard: What is logged
documents.text:
## What is logged
Production servers, network devices and identity systems log security-relevant events, including sign-ins, privilege changes and access to customer data. Company laptops send endpoint security events to the endpoint protection console.

documents.title: Halden Labs Logging and Monitoring Standard: Where logs go
documents.text:
## Where logs go
All production and network logs are forwarded to a central log platform. Engineers cannot delete or edit forwarded logs.

documents.title: Halden Labs Logging and Monitoring Standard: Retention
documents.text:
## Retention
Security event logs are retained for 90 days in the central log platform and then deleted.

documents.title: Halden Labs Logging and Monitoring Standard: Monitoring
documents.text:
## Monitoring
Network and service availability is monitored around the clock, with alerts paged to the on-call engineer. Security alerts from the log platform are triaged by the Security & IT team every business day.

documents.title: Halden Labs Incident Response Plan: Documented procedures
documents.text:
## Documented procedures
This plan documents how Halden Labs detects, triages, contains, investigates and recovers from security incidents. It is tested in a tabletop exercise twice a year.

documents.title: Halden Labs Incident Response Plan: Investigation
documents.text:
## Investigation
Halden Labs maintains an internal incident response team with forensics tooling and can conduct investigations without outside help. An external forensics firm is on retainer for major incidents.

documents.title: Halden Labs Incident Response Plan: Evidence
documents.text:
## Evidence
To support investigations, security logs are retained for 12 months.

documents.title: Halden Labs Incident Response Plan: Customer notification
documents.text:
## Customer notification
Affected customers are notified without undue delay, and in any case within 72 hours of confirming a security incident that affects their data.

documents.title: Halden Labs Incident Response Plan: Vulnerability reports
documents.text:
## Vulnerability reports
External researchers can report vulnerabilities to security@halden.example. Reports are acknowledged within two business days and triaged by the Security & IT team.

documents.title: Halden Labs Infrastructure Security Standard: Hosting
documents.text:
## Hosting
The Halden platform runs entirely in a major public cloud provider's data centers. Halden Labs does not operate its own data centers; physical security of those facilities is the provider's responsibility and is covered by the provider's SOC 2 report.

documents.title: Halden Labs Infrastructure Security Standard: Network
documents.text:
## Network
Cloud security groups and a managed web application firewall restrict inbound and outbound traffic. Internet-facing services sit in a separate public subnet; databases and internal services run in private subnets with no public addresses.
All traffic between services is encrypted with TLS 1.2 or higher, including traffic inside the private network. The TLS configuration is reviewed every quarter and only modern cipher suites are enabled.
Employees reach internal tools through a zero-trust access proxy. Halden Labs does not operate a traditional VPN.

documents.title: Halden Labs Infrastructure Security Standard: Hardening and patching
documents.text:
## Hardening and patching
Servers are built from hardened, versioned images defined in code. Security patches are applied monthly. Critical vulnerabilities are patched within 72 hours under an emergency change.

documents.title: Halden Labs Infrastructure Security Standard: Backups
documents.text:
## Backups
Production databases are backed up continuously to a second cloud region. Restores are tested every quarter.

documents.title: Halden Labs Infrastructure Security Standard: Testing
documents.text:
## Testing
An independent firm performs a manual penetration test of the platform once a year. Automated vulnerability scans of all production hosts run weekly.

documents.title: Halden Labs Infrastructure Security Standard: Change management
documents.text:
## Change management
Production changes go through a documented change process. Changes are classified as standard, normal or emergency by impact, and every change record is retained.

documents.title: Halden Labs Endpoint and Vendor Security Policy: Company devices
documents.text:
## Company devices
All company laptops are managed by the device management platform, have full-disk encryption turned on and run endpoint malware protection.
Phones may access company email only after enrolment in device management, which enforces device encryption and a passcode. Unenrolled or unencrypted mobile devices are blocked.

documents.title: Halden Labs Endpoint and Vendor Security Policy: Vendors
documents.text:
## Vendors
The Security & IT team reviews every service provider that will store or process customer data before contract signature, and again every year.
Contracts with these providers require them to protect the security and confidentiality of customer data at least to the standard of this program.

b.quote: Have you recently reviewed your SSL configuration to ensure that only secure protocols and ciphers are offered to clients?

request.query: Does the application enforce minimum password security requirements (e.g., a certain length, character classes, etc.)?

documents.text: Do you have an easily discoverable way for external researchers to report security vulnerabilities in your systems?
Have you recently reviewed your SSL configuration to ensure that only secure protocols and ciphers are offered to clients?
Does the application enforce minimum password security requirements (e.g., a certain length, character classes, etc.)?
Do user sessions in your application expire automatically when the user is inactive?
Are firewalls used at network boundaries to restrict inbound and outbound traffic?

Is encryption and integrity protection in place for all internal network traffic that potentially carries sensitive information (including passwords, emails, files, source code, management traffic, etc.)?
Have you implemented monitoring and alerting for your network?
Do you have a process for installing operating system and application updates and security patches on servers?
Do you also have an emergency process for installing patches outside of the regular patching schedule when high-risk vulnerabilities are identified?
Are your systems configured to log security-relevant events, such as authentication, data access, etc.?
Do you retain security event logs for at least 30 days?
Do your Windows domain administrators have separate accounts with lower privileges that they use for day-to-day tasks?
Do you have procedures in place for regularly auditing administrative access to your servers?
Do you store backup media in an off-site facility that is protected against potential disaster?
Do you regularly test your backups?
Do you have controls in place to protect client systems from malware?
Are laptops and other portable devices protected with full-disk encryption?
Do you allow access to confidential information (e.g., email) from unencrypted mobile devices such as phones and tablets?
Does an independent third party regularly perform penetration tests on all systems used to provide services to customers?
Do you run vulnerability scans at least once a year?
Does your company have a strong, established security program, and does the scope of the program include all information processed as part of this project?
Is a named person or team accountable for your information security and privacy program?
How often are internal information security and privacy audits performed?

Has your company selected an individual or team to be responsible for reviewing service providers and subcontractors, to ensure that they sufficiently protect the security and privacy of sensitive information and systems?
Is your change management process formally documented, and does it classify changes by impact and size?
Do you have documented procedures for responding to security incidents?
Do you inform affected customers about security incidents?

Do you have processes in place to ensure that access to data is granted solely on a "need-to-know" basis, in accordance with the job descriptions and responsibilities of users? Do these processes also revoke access when the need no longer exists?
Do you have processes in place to make sure access (both physical and logical) is revoked when an employee, intern, vendor, contractor, or other associate leaves the company or a contract ends?
Do employees receive security training when they join?
